If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset bearish pressure.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending down, add 0.3–0.7% upward correction in mid horizon (8–14 days) to counteract sentiment-induced overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending up, reduce 0.3–0.7% in mid horizon (8–14 days) to prevent overbought bias.

In late horizon (15–30 days), if sentiment is positive, apply 0.2–0.5% upward bias to align with sustained bullish sentiment; if negative, apply 0.2–0.5% downward bias to reflect bearish persistence.

If forecast deviates >1.5% from true value in any horizon and sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 0.5% correction in the next forecast step to reduce residual drift.
